title: A single generic ‘Preserve editorial intent’ prompt failed to stop editorial-hierarchy drift — empirical evidence from a controlled prompt-change test
description: In Experiment 005, adding one generic Narrative-user prompt section telling the agent to “preserve editorial intent” did not preserve the intended top-level company message. Controlled runs show the candidate prompt consistently subordinated Nuëyon’s company identity and audience while making orchestration the central positioning, and it introduced unsupported assertions — demonstrating that a generic preservation rule, by itself, can be insufficient.
audience: Product managers, prompt engineers, and editorial leads responsible for AI-driven content workflows and prompt governance.
rationale: Why it matters: Teams often try lightweight, reusable instructions to protect high-level editorial priorities. This experiment provides concrete evidence that a single generic preservation clause can fail, producing consistent but undesired editorial drift and unsupported claims. That makes the case for more precise, context-aware constraints or additional validation checks before promotion. Key gaps/uncertainties: the experiment used three runs per condition (not statistically rigorous), there was no seed/temperature control, and the provider/backend alias may have changed — so the result is strong for this controlled instance but not a universal proof. The idea can be developed into guidance on what to change next (e.g., more specific constraints, automated checks), but specifics of successful replacements are outside the source.
evidence: Controlled comparison: baseline Narrative mean 6.00/10 vs candidate 4.00/10; Compose baseline mean 5.67/10 vs candidate 3.33/10. All three candidate Narrative runs scored 0–1 on criterion C (theme hierarchy) and introduced unsupported audience/validation framing (criterion D failed in every candidate run). The candidate prompt added one section titled “Preserve Editorial Intent from the Synthesis” but contained only generic instructions; diff stored at prompt-changes/Narrative.user.prompt.diff. Decision: Do not promote; production prompt restored byte-for-byte.
